html:
The Massachusetts Bay Colony was an English colony on the coast of New England, founded in 1630 by Puritans led by John Winthrop. Its capital was Boston. The map shows it in 1650 and 1700.

It began with the Puritan migration of the 1630s, when some 20,000 English people came to New England to build a godly community. Church members ran the government, dissenters such as Anne Hutchinson were expelled, and the colony founded Harvard College in 1636. Farming families, fishing and trade with the West Indies made it prosper.

Its growth pressed on the Native peoples of the region, such as the Massachusett and the Wampanoag. In King Philip's War of 1675 to 1676 the colonists crushed the Wampanoag and their allies after heavy losses on both sides.

The Crown cancelled its charter in 1684. In 1691 a new charter joined it with Plymouth Colony as the Province of Massachusetts Bay, and the next year came the Salem witch trials. It became a leader of the revolt against Britain in the 1770s, part of British North America until then.
